v.why: Removing a 3x3 conv on the edge into the output deletes the main learnable feature path, so it hurts far more than removing a parameter-free edge (exp 1, 18 vs 49).
Replacing an avg-pool on the direct input-to-output edge with a conv removes a harmful smoothing shortcut and adds capacity, giving large gains (exp 8, 22).
Swapping a 3x3 conv for pooling on the direct input-output edge loses a key conv path and degrades accuracy much more than swapping a skip (exp 32, 86 vs 11, 95).
When edge 2->3 is absent, edge 1->3 is one of few routes to the output, so putting a conv there matters much more (exp 42, 67).
If the path into node 1 already has a 3x3 conv, the cell already has learnable capacity, so adding another conv on edge 5 yields smaller gains (exp 24 vs 13, 30, 39).
Removing edge 0 hurts more when it carries a conv than when it is a skip, which is nearly redundant with edge 3 (exp 5 vs 25, 55, 88).
With no direct input-output edge, information must flow through node 2, so a conv on edge 1 contributes more (exp 23, 53 vs 59, 69, 93).
Replacing a conv on edge 1->3 with parameter-free pooling removes capacity, whereas replacing a skip or none changes little.
When edge 5 is cut, the direct edge 0->3 carries more of the output signal, so making it a conv gives a bigger boost (exp 17).
Turning a 3x3 conv into an identity on the final edge sacrifices learnable capacity, while replacing pooling or none with skip is neutral or positive (exp 6, 56).
